extracted.intended_audience: reporters, editors, and other journalists covering trans people and related topics
extracted.subtask_description: A journalism style and coverage guide for reporters and editors on accurate, ethical, and nuanced reporting about trans people across beats (breaking news, health, sports, criminal justice, visual media, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: self-identification is paramount
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to determine a person's gender, name, and pronouns is to ask them directly. Police reports, public documents, or statements from family members can incorrectly identify someone. Social media profiles can be one clue, but they can also be misleading, outdated, incomplete, or falsified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take extra care during breaking news, which commonly misidentifies transgender people. Where possible and safe, ask sources for pronouns and self-identification; honor self-identification whenever possible. See specific topical guidance for breaking news.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'trans issues' is a euphemism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid collapsing anti-trans sentiment, laws, and policies into a single catch-all phrase like 'trans issues.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting on anti-trans politics benefits from clarity and specificity — e.g., civil rights protections, health care access, identity documents. Ask what the specific 'trans issue' is in a story and let that guide language; lay out the stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: talk to trans people about trans people
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on issues affecting trans communities, reporters should interview trans people who have relevant knowledge, experience, and expertise. Trans people's voices should be centered in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers who study trans communities may be trans themselves. Avoid building framing solely on cisgender sources’ voices and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: talk to trans people about things besides trans people
rubrics_metrics.description: Include trans people in sourcing for stories across beats; gender identity is just one part of a person and not the only thing that defines them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a gender-diverse sourcing pool and interview trans people for topics unrelated to gender when appropriate (professional expertise, academic work).

rubrics_metrics.name: take care not to ask irrelevant or unnecessary questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bring up transgender people's medical choices and personal histories unless directly relevant to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask only details that are clearly relevant. Refer to general less-extractive reporting best practices (e.g., 'Why Should I Tell You?: A Guide to Less-Extractive Reporting').

rubrics_metrics.name: never out sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not out trans people in reporting. Ensure sources understand implications of being identified as trans and clarify whether sensitive information is on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some people may be out in some contexts but not wish to be identified in searchable media reports. Respect requests for different names or pronouns for publication; prioritize safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: there is no single 'trans community'
rubrics_metrics.description: Trans communities are diverse across race, ethnicity, age, ability, nationality, location, politics, religion, tribal membership, economic background, and more; do not treat one person as representative of 'the trans experience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek diverse sources across these dimensions, just as with any other coverage area.

rubrics_metrics.name: trans terms and identities vary across cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-English languages have gender-related terms that are not equivalent to 'transgender' and should not be translated simplistically; identities and gender-neutral language vary widely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult experts and individuals from those communities. Avoid assuming equivalence across languages (example: travesti). See resources for reporting on gender minorities globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: be aware of slurs and other inflammatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow best practices for reprinting slurs (only in direct quotation, only when necessary for comprehension, and only with newsroom leadership approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Few quotations should pass this bar. Other inflammatory terms may require editorial consideration and fact-checking; consult the guide on politicized or inaccurate language for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: consult broader industry best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Because trans stories cross beats, reporters should consult relevant specialized reporting guidance (healthcare, trauma, education, etc.) in addition to this stylebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Association for Health Care Journalists for health stories; Dart Center for Journalism and Trauma for gun violence or trauma-informed reporting; Education Writers Association for stories involving trans youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: don’t guess anyone’s gender identity or pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume someone's gender identity or pronouns from appearance, presentation, pronouns in other contexts, or name. Ask all sources for pronouns and self-identification where safe/practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make asking pronouns routine, especially on beats likely to involve LGBTQ+ people. See self-identification guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: do not call unnecessary attention to a trans person’s gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not identify someone as transgender unless it provides necessary and relevant clarity or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters rarely note cisgender people's gender; similarly, avoid mentioning a subject is trans unless integral to understanding the story. Be concise when defining terms like 'nonbinary' only if the audience likely needs it.

rubrics_metrics.name: use current name/pronouns when writing about someone's past
rubrics_metrics.description: Use someone's current name and pronouns when writing about their past unless they request otherwise; omit, write around, or bracket out deadnaming/misgendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a trans person requests to deadname/misgender themself in a quote about the past, publish verbatim only if it adds value and is clearly consented to. Don't use outdated name/pronouns outside direct quotation unless directed by the person.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid 'identifies as' phrasing for gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write 'identifies as a man/woman/nonbinary' about people; simply state that someone is a man, woman, nonbinary, trans, etc., unless directly quoting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels how one would not write 'identifies as a man' for cisgender people; the phrasing implies distance or doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: never publish a deadname without express permission
rubrics_metrics.description: A deadname is a name a trans person no longer uses; do not publish it without explicit permission as it can be offensive and dangerous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadname is not interchangeable with legal name; high-profile figures may have complicated relationships with deadnames. Ask what language individuals prefer if a story must refer to former names. Never knowingly deadname a trans person in obituaries or posthumous coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: when past news coverage deadnames/misgenders someone — update only in limited cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not proactively update past stories when someone changes name/gender unless (1) the person was identified incorrectly when published (reporting error) or (2) the person was identified correctly at publication but has since changed identity and requested a retroactive update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correcting an error, issue a correction note without restating the incorrect info. If updating by request, honor according to newsroom standards and possibly add a brief editor's note (not a correction) stating the report was updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: update web assets that deadname/misgender when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-story backend assets (taxonomy tags, alt-text) may contain deadnames or outdated info; update these when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redirect old tags to current names and tag future coverage appropriately, even if the source hasn't contacted you — they may not know the assets exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: do not publish verbatim quotes that deadname or misgender a subject — bracket or paraphrase
rubrics_metrics.description: When sources (family, friends, public figures, documents) deadname/misgender someone, do not publish the quote verbatim; use brackets to replace incorrect information or paraphrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that the person was being deadnamed/misgendered if it provides helpful context (example provided). See Photography and Visual Media for multimedia approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: pronoun basics — ask and respect published pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: When interviewing a trans source, ask which pronouns they want published and respect that choice. Some may request different pronouns for publication than in person for safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pronouns normally in stories; do not write around pronouns to avoid singular they. There is never a reason to explain standard they/them, he/him, she/her in copy unless context requires clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: use gender-neutral and neopronoun language respectfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate language to describe they/them and other gender-neutral neopronouns (ze/hir, ey/em); do not substitute they/them automatically for neopronouns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure of spelling or usage of a neopronoun, ask the person. Provide brief explanatory phrasing for less common pronouns when useful (e.g., 'Taylor, who uses ze/hir pronouns').

rubrics_metrics.name: respect multiple pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people use multiple sets of pronouns (e.g., he/they). Ask which pronouns to publish and respect whether they prefer one or multiple to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be appropriate to explain use of multiple pronouns in an appositive or editor’s note depending on story/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid the phrase 'preferred pronouns'
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use 'preferred pronouns' because pronouns are not a preference but the appropriate way to refer to someone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase is only appropriate when someone uses more than one set of pronouns and explicitly indicates a preference among them.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular they/them usage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular they is standard usage (takes plural verb); reflexive can be 'themself' or 'themselves' with 'themself' often clearer for a single person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No need to explain the use of singular they in copy. Ensure clarity in sentences to avoid confusing singular/plural reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: what to do if you can’t determine someone’s pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not avoid using a person’s name or pronouns simply because they are transgender or nonbinary. Write around pronouns only if it is impossible to determine the right pronoun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some outlets use singular they as a substitute; others prefer writing around pronouns or gendered identifications entirely. Choose approach according to newsroom style and safety concerns (e.g., unidentified person, unclear identity, breaking news).

rubrics_metrics.name: use 'assigned sex at birth' not 'born female/born male' when precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned sex at birth clarifies that sex and gender labels are given by others at birth; assigned sex refers to anatomy whereas assigned gender refers to how infants are labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrases like 'born female' or 'born a girl.' Use AMAB/AFAB where it provides useful specificity for health/legal contexts, but do not apply assigned-sex labels to individuals who do not use them. In nonhuman contexts, use 'sex' (male/female).

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid using 'biological sex' carelessly
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside medical literature, 'assigned sex at birth' is preferable. 'Biological sex' is politicized and used by some to imply immutable sex; its meaning varies by jurisdiction and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When covering policy, quote legal language directly and explain how a law defines 'biological sex.' Avoid using 'biological' to describe people (e.g., 'biological women') and avoid uncritically reprinting speculation about individuals' birth sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid vague political jargon like 'culture war' as a substitute for specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'culture war' sparingly and only in very sweeping references; avoid using it as a euphemism for debates that are specifically about trans or LGBTQ+ people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what is being debated (e.g., restricting access to health care for trans minors) and fact-check claims about prevalence/content of 'culture war' narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid labeling people as 'detransitioners' outside direct quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: While describing a person’s choice to detransition is acceptable, avoid the label 'detransitioner' except in direct quotes because it can be offensive and politicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume reasons for stopping transition-related care; report on individual circumstances with nuance and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid the charged term 'gender ideology' — use neutral phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Gender ideology' is a charged term used by anti-trans commentators; refer instead to 'trans identity' or 'being transgender.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate with 'gender-critical' ideologies; prefer neutral descriptive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: do not use 'gender nonbinary' (grammatically incorrect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'gender nonbinary' is grammatically incorrect (analogous to 'gender woman'); use conventions like 'nonbinary' or 'a nonbinary person.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep definitions concise and only include them when the audience needs clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: treat 'groomer' accusations as serious criminal accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusations of grooming imply child sexual abuse and should be treated with that level of seriousness; vague use as an insult is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If quoting someone using the term, be clear whether they mean it rhetorically or allege proven abuse; if alleging abuse, add necessary details. Beware of baseless claims that rely only on a person's queer/trans status.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid terms like 'male-bodied' or 'female-bodied'
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms like 'male-bodied' and 'female-bodied' are reductive and often pejorative references to assigned sex; avoid them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize body diversity and avoid framing bodies solely by assigned sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid repeating loaded terms like 'mutilation' and 'sterilization' without fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents of transgender medical care use 'mutilation' and 'sterilization' as rhetorical devices; these claims are often inaccurate (e.g., hormone therapy does not guarantee infertility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check and avoid uncritical repetition; provide context on what medical care for minors typically entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid 'opposite sex' or 'opposite gender' phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases like 'opposite sex' reinforce a strict binary and inaccurately position genders as opposites; avoid them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more precise language that does not reify a binary opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: treat 'rapid-onset gender dysphoria/social contagion' claims as debunked
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapid-onset gender dysphoria is a debunked theory; when quoting claims that reference it, clarify there is no evidence to support the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note corrections and the scholarly consensus rejecting the theory; avoid amplifying misinformation without context.

rubrics_metrics.name: do not assess whether someone 'passes' or is 'stealth' based on reporters' observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not describe someone as 'stealth' or evaluate whether they 'pass' from a journalist’s own observation; these terms may be acceptable when used as direct quotes from the person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, allow sources to describe themselves using these terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid terms that suggest 'transgenderism' or 'trans ideology'
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms like 'transgenderism,' 'trans ideology,' or 'trans agenda' are loaded and imply a political philosophy; use neutral terms like 'transness' or 'transgender identity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to activists, be specific: 'trans health care advocates' rather than generalized labels. Do not call 'transgender' a noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: do not use 'transgendered' — prefer 'transgender' or 'trans'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Transgendered' is outdated and offensive; use 'transgender' as an adjective and 'trans' as shorthand. Do not use 'transgender' as a noun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer neutral constructions such as 'being transgender' or 'trans identity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: be precise about 'trans activists' vs people who are simply trans
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not conflate being openly trans with being an activist; identify someone as an activist only if they engage in political action or self-describe as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific descriptors (e.g., 'trans health care advocates') rather than broad or pejorative labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: use 'anti-trans' modifier rather than casual use of 'TERF' unless quoted/specified
rubrics_metrics.description: TERF (trans-exclusionary radical feminist) is a contested label; prefer describing beliefs/actions directly or use 'anti-trans' when referring to anti-trans rhetoric or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reprinting TERF or related terms, define and provide context. Avoid using TERF as a general interchangeable term.

rubrics_metrics.name: breaking news: identifying transgender people
rubrics_metrics.description: Be especially careful in breaking news to avoid misidentification; consult guide on identifying transgender people during breaking news and on what to do if self-identification cannot be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write around outdated or false details; practice trauma-informed reporting; follow specific guidance for publishing identifying information about trans children and reporting on deaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: publish identifying information about trans children only with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing identifying information about trans children carries heightened safety concerns and requires careful editorial consideration and reference to education/youth-specific guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Education Writers Association guidance and newsroom policy; prioritize child safety and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: reporting on the deaths of trans people — trauma-informed and contextual
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting deaths of trans people, be trauma-informed, avoid sensationalism, and beware of misgendering or deadnaming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow best practices for trauma-informed journalism and consult the topical guide on reporting on crimes and violent deaths involving trans people.

rubrics_metrics.name: anti-trans laws and policies — focus on tangible effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering anti-trans laws and policies, explain what the policy does and its concrete effects rather than only technical legal language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote legal language where necessary, but use less technical language outside legal reporting. Describe specific allegations when alleging discrimination rather than relying on abstract legal phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: reporting on U.S. trans health care bans — specialized guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on health-care-related bans, follow the health-care topical guidance and consult specialized industry resources for medical context and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include context about what care entails, age-dependence, and how policies affect access to care.

rubrics_metrics.name: criminal justice reporting — avoid amplifying anti-trans misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be attentive to anti-trans misinformation around mass shootings and extremist activities; when reporting on crimes involving trans people, provide accurate context and avoid misattributing motive based on gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider interplay between gender identity and carceral policy; follow guidance on reporting on incarcerated trans people and identifying trans sources in prisons or jails.

rubrics_metrics.name: health care reporting — use precise and non-stigmatizing language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use accurate language for transgender health care, prefer gender-neutral medical language where appropriate, and only include protected health information when necessary to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful around detransition/retransition coverage; contextualize hormone therapy and reproductive health; consult health-care reporting best practices (Association for Health Care Journalists).

rubrics_metrics.name: sports reporting — use nuanced definitions and avoid umbrella traps
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on trans people in sports, be precise about the specific issue (youth vs elite competition, testosterone regulations, competitive advantage claims) and recognize 'transgender athletes' is an umbrella term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid broad, sensational headlines; explain rules/regulations and provide evidence for claims about advantage. Cite relevant governing bodies and scientific evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: drag coverage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context when reporting on drag and avoid conflating drag performance with the identities of trans people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about distinctions and respectful of cultures and histories of drag scenes; avoid sensationalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: describing how trans people look — avoid focusing on physicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid unnecessary descriptions of trans people's appearance or physical characteristics that are not relevant to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appearance is newsworthy, be measured and respectful; avoid language that reduces people to physical traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: obituaries — do not deadname or misgender
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not knowingly deadname or misgender deceased trans people; use current name/pronouns and respect requests from families/sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to privacy and safety concerns even in posthumous coverage. Follow dedicated obituaries guidance in the stylebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: reporting on asylum seekers/refugees and sex work — use specialized, respectful framing
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering asylum seekers/refugees or sex work involving trans people, apply domain-specific best practices to avoid exploitation and harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about vulnerabilities, legal frameworks, and safety; consult specialized guides and community experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid the 'losing a loved one' cliche
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid clichéd phrasing like 'losing a loved one' when it flattens nuanced experiences in reporting about trans people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek more precise and humanizing language; consider how cliches may minimize or misframe experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: understanding polling data — interpret carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting polling that involves trans people or related policy questions, interpret methodology, sampling, and question wording carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about what the poll actually measures, margins of error, and limitations in questions about gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: obscure information that could endanger sources (visual media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish visual information that could identify or endanger sources (locations, easily searchable identifiers) in photos or videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blur, crop, or otherwise obscure identifying details as necessary. Consider security implications for trans sources, especially those at risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: obtain informed consent from subjects for visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Get informed consent from people depicted in photographs, video, or other visual media, especially when identity disclosure could cause harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how images will be used, distributed, and archived; obtain explicit consent for publishing identifying images of trans people.

rubrics_metrics.name: remove deadnames or misgendering from visual assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure captions, metadata, alt-text, and other visual asset descriptors do not deadname or misgender subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update backend assets when people change names/pronouns; check file names, metadata, and stock-image labels for outdated information.

rubrics_metrics.name: use file photos with care
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using stock or file images that may misrepresent or endanger subjects (e.g., photos that stereotype or reveal identifying details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for inappropriate stock images; avoid imagery that reinforces stereotypes or reveals sensitive information about individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: watch for inappropriate stock images
rubrics_metrics.description: Be attentive to stock images that caricature or stereotype trans people or that use voyeuristic or sexualized imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose images that respect subjects' dignity and accurately reflect story context. Consider commissioning appropriate photography when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: use glossary terms accurately and respect self-identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use glossary definitions (e.g., trans, nonbinary, gender dysphoria, Two-Spirit) as guidance, but honor how individuals self-describe when the stylebook is silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that lexicon is dynamic; the guide is not comprehensive. When uncertain, ask sources how they describe themselves and follow their lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: honor diversity of language and evolving terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that terminology evolves and some community-preferred terms may conflict with the guide; prioritize individuals' stated language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive revisions are made quarterly; when guidance is silent, honor the way someone speaks about themself whenever possible. Contact the style guide editor for unresolved issues.
